slides.say: Five different positive whole numbers have a sum of twenty. Which of the following must be true?

Must be true means true in every allowed case. So one allowed case where a choice fails is enough to rule it out. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways, by plugging in numbers to break the choices, and then by understanding why the last one always holds.
[short pause] Let's start by plugging in numbers. The smallest five different positive numbers are one, two, three, four and five. Together that's fifteen, so five more are left to give out.

Choice number two says the largest number is at most nine. To break it, we give all five extras to the largest. Five plus five is ten. So one, two, three, four and ten add up to twenty, and the largest is ten. That's not at most nine, so choice number two is out.
at: So one, two, three, four and ten
so choice number two is out

slides.say: Choice number one says one of the numbers is one. To break it, we give one extra to every number. Two, three, four, five and six. That's still twenty, and there's no one. So choice number one is out.
at: Two, three, four, five and six
So choice number one is out

slides.say: Choice number three says at least two of the numbers are even. Let's try to have only one even number, like one, three, four, five and seven. One plus three is four. Four plus four is eight. Eight plus five is thirteen. And thirteen plus seven is twenty. Only four is even, so choice number three is out.
at: so choice number three is out

slides.say: Choice number four is the only one left. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] In the exam you'd stop there. But let's see why choice number four must be true. It says the largest number is at least six. That's a minimum and maximum question. How small can the largest number be?

Say the largest were five or less. Then all five numbers are different, positive, and at most five. There's only one way to do that, one, two, three, four and five. Their sum is fifteen, not twenty. So the largest can't be five or less, and it must be at least six.
at: Say the largest were five or less

slides.say: And six really happens, with two, three, four, five and six. So it's true in every allowed case. Choice number four is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
